messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert — elevated 5xx error rate and latency on /v1/generate (redwood-large-v2-q4) in us-east-1; error spike started ~2799991087; paging oncall. Autotriggered runbook: model-canary-failure.

SRE Pager: I'm on it. grabbing logs and initiating warm fallback check. @Alice Ramos can you confirm whether this was a scheduled canary rollout?

Alice Ramos: yes — we pushed redwood-large-v2-q4 (quantized) into 10% canary at ~2799991000 for lower token cost; no canary alerts during smoke on dry-run.

Ben Kim: I see increased tail latency and a pattern of `kv-cache-miss` entries in the runtime logs right before 503s. Sharing tail of logs here:```
[2799991085] runtime: seq_len=2048, alloc_kv=miss
[2799991086] runtime: eval_batch_alloc failed: OOM?
[2799991086] model: redwood-large-v2-q4 shard0: response aborted 503
[2799991087] router: fallback to redwood-large-v2 fallback-variant
```

Priya Nair: Customer impact: external error rate up 2.1% overall for /v1/generate; several PLG customers reported degraded responses (timeouts and partial responses). DataDog chart pinned here: <https://datadog.company/mon/abc123|canary-5xx-us-east-1> :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Jordan Li: Deploy bot shows the rollout was triggered by marketplace-pack: `deploy 2026-10-12T18:30 -> redwood-large-v2-q4 @ canary=10%`. I can run diff between canary and baseline metrics for last hour. Running quick compare...

DataDogBot: quick-compare results attached — latency p95 increased by 320ms on canary bucket; error rate in canary cohort 6.4% vs baseline 0.2%.

Maya Patel: We need to decide rollback vs pin. Current traffic: 10% canary. Is the fallback path (autofallback to baseline) working reliably? Any request replays causing double billing?

Ben Kim: Autofallback is partially working — router logs show intermittent fallbacks but not consistent. Some requests still get routed to the canary shard and fail before fallback triggers. Looks like a KV cache initialization race under specific long-context loads.

SRE Pager: Immediate mitigation options in runbook: 1) Increase fallback weight to 0% (effectively pin to baseline) 2) Pause rollout (stop further canary expansion) 3) Rollback canary and pin to previous model. We should assess probability of rollback impact (latency/cost rollback to baseline).

Alice Ramos: I'm going to pause the canary expansion (deploy-bot: `pause rollout redwood-large-v2-q4`) and increase router fallback weight. 

deploy-bot: command accepted — rollout paused at 10%. Router fallback weight set to prefer baseline variant.

Priya Nair: Noting customer-impact timeline: first 5xxs at ~2799991087; support tickets opened at ~2799991120; major PLG customer #42 reported partial tokens at ~2799991145. Ticket links: <https://support.company/tickets/9981>, <https://support.company/tickets/9982>.

Jordan Li: Sharing canary vs baseline diffs:```
metric: p95_latency | baseline: 240ms | canary: 560ms
metric: error_rate | baseline: 0.2% | canary: 6.4%
trace sample (canary): failed at runtime shard0 -> kv-init -> out-of-bounds mem access
```

Ben Kim: Hypothesis A: quantized kernel path for q4 variant has a memory regression under long-context sequences causing intermittent allocation failures and incomplete writes -> 503s. Hypothesis B: runtime change that interacts with compile/kernel selection causing rare path. Hypothesis C: upstream routing cutoff misconfiguration causing partial responses. Prioritize A and test locally with reproduced seq_len=2048 load.

Alice Ramos: I have a repro harness. Running load test with seq_len=2048 and batch sizes matching production; will spin up instrumented canary shard to capture full core dumps. ETA ~12 minutes.

DataDogBot: additional anomalies — GC pauses correlated with error spikes, node-level memory usage spike at 80% before failure.

Maya Patel: While we validate, recommend full rollback for safety if we can't get deterministic repro within 20 minutes. Customer ops wants a clear statement for PLG customers.

SRE Pager: Agreed. But before rollback, let's ensure we didn't leave pinned tokens or partial logs. Action items: - @Jordan capture canary kv cache metrics and heapdumps - @Ben run repro load against q4 locally and post results - @Alice collect core dumps and attach to thread - @Maya prepare customer comms draft.

Jordan Li: KV metrics attached: `kv_init_time` spikes, `kv_cache_misses` up 14x. Heapdump links: <s3://internal/heaps/279999-cork1> (instrumented).

Ben Kim: Local repro started. Running 200 concurrent requests with seq_len=2048. First failures at 2:45 into test, reproducing the same stacktrace. Posting snippet:```
runtime: alloc_kv failed at 0x7f9b23c -> return EFAULT
model: aborting response -> 503
```

Alice Ramos: Core dumps uploaded: <s3://internal/cores/279999-core-01>. Preliminary analysis: memcopy in quantized kernel touches OOB under alignment shift for long sequences. Looks like a bounds-check regression introduced in model compilation layer.

Maya Patel: Given repro and core, I'm drafting rollback notice. We'll perform coordinated rollback to stable variant `redwood-large-v2` at 2799991300 UTC if no objections. Customer messaging: acknowledge degraded responses, mitigation in progress, ETA for fix TBD.

Priya Nair: Support staffing: two senior SEs on chat, PS will prepare one-off replays for top impacted customers. Logging bucket for affected requests: `rb-279999-canary-err`.

Ben Kim: Recommendation: full rollback now. Patch window could take longer to compile and validate. Risk of leaving canary at 10% is continued customer impact.

Alice Ramos: I concur. Initiating rollback via deploy-bot: `rollback redwood-large-v2-q4 -> redwood-large-v2 stable` and pin baseline.

deploy-bot: rollback started. Initiating gradual drain of canary sessions, re-route new requests to baseline. Expected completion ~2799991390.

incident-bot: Note: runbook step executed: rollback to stable triggered by oncall at 2799991335. Please update incident timeline and next steps.

DataDogBot: Post-rollback quick-check: error rate falling — canary cohort errors down to 0.4% within 3m, overall /v1/generate errors back to 0.3%.

SRE Pager: Ok stabilizing. Next actions for RCA thread: - Build timeline (we have timestamps for alert, rollout, first 5xx, pause, rollback) - Share diffs and core analysis (Ben/Alice/Jordan) - Root cause hypothesis: quantized kernel bounds-check regression in compilation -> causes OOB on long-contexts. - Remediation plan: revert kernel change in compiler, add unit/regression tests for seq_len=2048 and alignment, improve canary gating to include long-context synthetic traffic.

Maya Patel: I'll schedule a cross-team RCA meeting at 2799991600 and prepare a customer update for impacted PLG customers by 2799991500.

Alice Ramos: Uploading a short reproduce script and the failing kernel snippet to the shared folder: <https://git.company/runs/279999/canary-repro>.

Ben Kim: Adding regression tests to repo and gating in compile pipeline. Will open PR referencing this incident.

Jordan Li: I'll prepare timeline doc and attach Datadog graphs + diff CSVs to the incident JIRA.

SRE Pager: Marking incident as mitigated for customer traffic; leaving thread open for RCA artifacts and postmortem. If any regressions pop back up, re-page. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. Runbook link: <https://runbooks.company/model-canary-failure>.

Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. Draft sent to legal and comms for review prior to sending to customers. I'll ping when ready.

Alice Ramos: final note — avoid expanding canaries without long-context synthetic tests; also recommend temporary increase in fallback sensitivity for quantized variants until fully validated.

Ben Kim: +1. Closing loop here, will follow up with PRs and the kernel revert.

SRE Pager: Thread summary for postmortem: alert -> canary 10% -> kv-cache/alloc regression -> partial fallbacks -> pause then rollback -> error rate back to baseline -> root cause suspected in quantized kernel alignment logic.

Maya Patel: Added postmortem placeholder ticket: INC-279999-rca. Assigning to Alice/Ben/Jordan for artifact uploads.

incident-bot: This thread will be archived when the postmortem is published. Thanks to responders: @Alice Ramos, @Ben Kim, @Priya Nair, @Jordan Li, @Maya Patel, @SRE Pager.
